output.technical_predicate: Ordinary case and offer routes (/case/{id} and /case/{id}/offer) must be reachable only by the authenticated owner or the assigned officer; any other borrower or unassigned officer must be denied.
applicability_facts: Scenario: synthetic EU-established private controller; risk is disclosure of a case or offer via its ordinary case and download routes; permitted principals are the owner and the assigned officer.
app.py:0068-0071 requires an authenticated session (who) before any case route is served.
app.py:0092-0095 parses /case/{cid} and resolves the case via store.get_case(db, who, cid).
store.py:0055-0058 get_case selects the row only WHERE id=? AND (owner=? OR officer=?), raising 404 otherwise — this is the single gate for both the detail route and the offer route.
app.py:0110-0112 serves the ordinary case detail (op is None) after get_case, with no further principal check.
app.py:0100-0103 serves /case/{id}/offer after get_case, gated only on stage in (accepted, offered) and not restricted — no additional principal check.
store.py:0111-0112 offer() returns case id, email, amount and term for the resolved case.
relevant_exceptions: No exception in the supplied source: get_case applies the owner-or-officer predicate unconditionally for every authenticated principal.
The offer route's stage/restriction checks (app.py:0102) are availability conditions, not principal exceptions.
The access/portable routes (app.py:0105) add an owner-only check, but that is outside the named case/offer routes.
required_controls: Owner-or-assigned-officer predicate in the case lookup (store.py:0056) applied to both /case/{id} and /case/{id}/offer.
Non-matching principals receive 404 'Case unavailable.' (store.py:0057), not the resource.
Offer payload only produced after the same lookup succeeds (app.py:0100-0103, store.py:0111-0112).
assessment_limits: Static reading of supplied source only; no execution, browsing or repository access was performed.
Officer assignment is fixed at submission (store.py:0076) mapping each customer to one officer; behavior for other officer accounts is inferred from the SQL predicate, not observed.
Session identity (who) is taken from the server-side session store (app.py:0044-0047); session-forgery or cookie-handling weaknesses were not analyzed.
Compliance conclusion is limited to the named case and offer routes; other routes (access, portable, transfer, campaign) are out of scope.
No legal deadline or penalty assessment is made.
